statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 21% as NQ futures reclaim the overnight low and trade near flat, while Stress stays high on the oil, yield and Fed-repricing backdrop.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Forecast Tail crosses the block threshold only inside the narrow 12:00-15:00 UTC window covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with a second single-hour checkpoint at the 21:00 UTC Broadcom call. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures reclaim the overnight low and hold near flat while oil and global yields stabilise
body: NQ futures traded near 29,106.75 at 07:16 UTC, about 0.06% below the 29,125.50 previous close, after printing an overnight low of 29,016.50 and recovering roughly 90 points from it. Two independent quote sources agree on the level and on the 29,016.50 low, and the session range of about 29,016.50-29,170.00 is now being traded two-way rather than extended one-way. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Sep 1 at 29,077.22, down 1.29%, in a 28,953.26-29,267.42 range, alongside the S&P 500 at 7,631.47 (-0.71%) and the Dow at 52,766.88 (-0.79%). The macro backdrop remains genuinely stressed but is no longer extending: Brent near $94.89 and WTI near $90.26 have eased from the $95.45 Asian-session high after Tuesday's roughly 5% surge on US strikes around the Strait of Hormuz, the US 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.798% after reaching its highest since January 2025, Japanese 10-year yields sit at their highest since 1996, UK 30-year yields at the highest since 1998, VIX closed at 16.34 after a 9.5% rise, and fed funds futures price better than a two-in-three chance of a rate increase at the September 16 FOMC meeting. Sep 1 sector performance was uniformly negative, with semiconductors near -1.4% and software groups down 2.5-3.0%. The decisive observation for Tail is that the Nasdaq has absorbed all of this without a no-retracement path: Asian cash equities fell 2-4% overnight, the KOSPI near -4% and the Nikkei near -2.9%, while NQ futures are close to unchanged and have reclaimed their own low. That is a high-Stress environment with multiple aligned cross-asset amplifiers, but the price path itself is two-way. Tail is therefore lowered to 21% from 23% and Stress to 72% from 75%. Confidence is 88% because current futures pricing from two sources, index levels, yields, oil, the Fed pricing backdrop and the verified event calendar were all obtained this cycle. The shared Finviz context file was older than the 90-minute freshness bound this run and was therefore not relied upon.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours opened calm, with Tail at 11% during the early European session on Sep 1. Tail then stepped up sharply from 08:00 UTC as the US-Iran escalation, the oil surge and the sovereign-yield selloff were priced in, peaking at 31% around the US cash open before easing back. The late US session and the Asian handover held Tail in a 20-25% band with Stress persistently high at 70-77%, describing a difficult but two-way environment rather than a sustained one-way trend. The last six published hours drifted between 20% and 23%. Three hourly slots have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 21-24% band for most of the next 24 hours and lifts it above the block threshold only for the three-hour catalyst cluster from 12:00 to 15:00 UTC, covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with the single highest reading of 28% in the 13:00 UTC hour that contains the opening auction. One further hour reaches the threshold at 21:00 UTC around Broadcom's earnings call, where a top-weight constituent can move the semiconductor complex in thin post-close futures. Stress stays high throughout on the oil, yield and Fed-repricing backdrop, which is structural rather than intraday, and eases only gradually overnight. Confidence decays with forecast distance because no live price-path evidence exists for later windows at the assessment cutoff.

forecast.analysis: Observed at the cutoff: NQ futures near 29,107, about 0.06% below the 29,125.5 previous close, after reclaiming an overnight low of 29,016.50 with a roughly 90-point recovery. That retracement, plus Brent easing to about $94.9, lowers Tail a little while the macro Stress backdrop stays high.
